packetdoctor.title: Packet Doctor
packetdoctor.title_button.tooltip: Packet warnings, disconnect and crash explanations, and settings
packetdoctor.section.technical: TECHNICAL DETAILS (for modders and server admins)
packetdoctor.saved_to: Report saved to: %s (click to open the folder)
packetdoctor.status.export_failed: Couldn't save the packet log (see the game log)
packetdoctor.status.connected: Connected to %s  ·  receiving %s packets/s  ·  sending %s packets/s
packetdoctor.status.not_connected: Not connected to a server right now.
packetdoctor.warnings.none: No problems found on this connection. ✔
packetdoctor.warnings.explain: Packet Doctor checks every packet between you and the server. If something could lag you, crash you or get you kicked, it shows up here with an explanation.
packetdoctor.live.empty: No packets yet. Join a world or server to see traffic.
packetdoctor.history.empty: Nothing yet. When you get disconnected or the game crashes, the explanation is kept here.
packetdoctor.history.hint: Click an entry to open its full explanation.
packetdoctor.settings.hint: Click a setting to change it. Changes are saved straight away.
packetdoctor.settings.toasts.desc: Show a small pop-up in the corner when a new problem is found.
packetdoctor.settings.toast_info.desc: Also pop up harmless notes, like data for mods you don't have or server transfers.
packetdoctor.settings.cooldown.desc: How long before the same problem can pop up again.
packetdoctor.settings.title_button.desc: Show the Packet Doctor button in the top-left of the title screen.
packetdoctor.settings.open_crash.desc: After a crash, open the explanation automatically when the game starts again.
packetdoctor.settings.log_size: Packets kept in the Live log
packetdoctor.settings.log_size.desc: This is also what Export log saves. More packets use a little more memory.
packetdoctor.settings.keep_reports.desc: Older report and export files are deleted automatically.
packetdoctor.source.server: The server (or one of its plugins)
packetdoctor.source.item_data: Items with a lot of data (e.g. huge books or shulker boxes)
packetdoctor.source.mismatch: A version or mod mismatch between you and the server
packetdoctor.who.world_or_items: Something in the world or an item
packetdoctor.error.npe: it tried to use something that wasn't there
packetdoctor.error.index: it looked past the end of a list
packetdoctor.error.cast: it mixed up two kinds of objects
packetdoctor.error.state: something was in an unexpected state
packetdoctor.error.argument: it was given a value it couldn't use
packetdoctor.note.server_confirmed: The server runs Packet Doctor too and confirmed this.
packetdoctor.note.error_in_mod: The error came from this mod's code.
packetdoctor.note.error_in_mod_handling: The error happened inside this mod while it handled the packet.
packetdoctor.note.decode_mod: This mod's code was reading the data when it failed.
packetdoctor.note.decode_channel: The broken data was on this mod's channel (%s).
packetdoctor.note.closed_mod: This mod sent the bad data just before the server closed the connection.
packetdoctor.note.seen_mod: Packet Doctor saw this mod cause "%s" just before.
packetdoctor.note.oom_mod: %s was running when memory ran out, but it may not be the one using it all.
packetdoctor.note.closest_mod: This mod's code was closest to the error.
packetdoctor.note.closest_mod_others: This mod's code was closest to the error (%s other mods were also involved).
packetdoctor.note.no_mod_in_error: No mod's code appears in the error, so it is most likely Minecraft itself or its settings.
packetdoctor.note.no_single_mod: No single mod could be identified.
packetdoctor.note.graphics_mod: This mod was drawing on screen when the graphics error happened.
packetdoctor.note.world_mod: This mod's code was running for the broken object.
packetdoctor.dc.kicked.headline: You were kicked
packetdoctor.dc.kicked.summary: Someone on the server (or one of its plugins) removed you. You can usually join again straight away.
packetdoctor.dc.banned.headline: You are banned from this server
packetdoctor.dc.banned.summary: The server has banned your account. You can't join until the ban ends or is lifted.
packetdoctor.dc.banned_ip.headline: Your internet address is banned
packetdoctor.dc.banned_ip.summary: The server has banned your IP address, so every account from your internet connection is blocked.
packetdoctor.dc.whitelist.headline: You aren't on this server's whitelist
packetdoctor.dc.whitelist.summary: This server only lets in players on its list, and your account isn't on it.
packetdoctor.dc.whitelist.note: The server's settings decide who can join.
packetdoctor.dc.full.headline: The server is full
packetdoctor.dc.full.summary: Every player slot is taken. Nothing is wrong with your game.
packetdoctor.dc.duplicate.headline: Your account logged in somewhere else
packetdoctor.dc.duplicate.summary: The same account joined this server from another place, so the older connection (this one) was removed.
packetdoctor.dc.duplicate.note: Only one connection per account is allowed.
packetdoctor.dc.idle.headline: You were idle for too long
packetdoctor.dc.idle.summary: The server removes players who don't move for a while.
packetdoctor.dc.flying.headline: The server thinks you were flying
packetdoctor.dc.flying.summary: You were in the air for too long without being allowed to fly. This is usually a movement mod, but heavy lag can cause it too.
packetdoctor.dc.invalid_move.headline: Your game sent an impossible position
packetdoctor.dc.invalid_move.summary: Your game told the server you were somewhere impossible (a broken number or outside the world). The server kicks for this to protect itself.
packetdoctor.dc.invalid_move.note: The bad position came from your game.
packetdoctor.dc.illegal_chars.headline: Your message had characters that aren't allowed
packetdoctor.dc.illegal_chars.summary: A chat message or command you sent contained an invisible or special character that Minecraft doesn't allow in chat.
packetdoctor.dc.illegal_chars.note: It usually comes from pasted text or a chat mod.
packetdoctor.dc.spam.headline: Kicked for chat spam
packetdoctor.dc.spam.summary: You sent chat messages or commands too quickly.
packetdoctor.dc.packet_rate.headline: Your game sent too much, too fast
packetdoctor.dc.packet_rate.summary: The server has a limit on how many packets a player may send each second, and your game went over it.%s
packetdoctor.dc.packet_rate.peak: The busiest second had %s packets, mostly: %s.
packetdoctor.dc.packet_rate.note: Usually a mod or macro that clicks, moves or interacts very quickly.
packetdoctor.dc.version.headline: Your game version doesn't match the server
packetdoctor.dc.version.summary: The server runs a different Minecraft version than you.%s
packetdoctor.dc.version.note: Both sides have to run versions that can talk to each other.
packetdoctor.dc.invalid_attack.headline: You attacked something you aren't allowed to
packetdoctor.dc.invalid_attack.summary: Your game tried to attack an entity that can't be attacked (for example yourself, an item or an arrow). This almost always comes from a combat mod.
packetdoctor.dc.invalid_attack.note: Most likely a combat or auto-attack mod.
packetdoctor.dc.chat_signing.headline: Chat signing failed
packetdoctor.dc.chat_signing.summary: Minecraft signs chat messages to prove who sent them, and %s found a problem with a signature. This is often a wrong computer clock, an expired login, or a chat mod.
packetdoctor.dc.missing_tags.headline: The server sent incomplete game data
packetdoctor.dc.missing_tags.summary: The server didn't send some of the data (tags) your game needs to load the world. This is a problem on the server side, often a plugin or datapack.
packetdoctor.dc.coc.headline: You didn't accept the server's rules
packetdoctor.dc.coc.summary: This server shows a code of conduct when you join, and it wasn't accepted.
packetdoctor.dc.transfers_disabled.headl: The server tried to send you to another server
packetdoctor.dc.transfers_disabled.summa: The server tried to move you to a different server%s, but the target doesn't accept transfers.
packetdoctor.dc.slow_login.headline: Logging in took too long
packetdoctor.dc.slow_login.summary: Your game took too long to finish joining, so the server gave up. Slow connections and very big modpacks can cause this.
packetdoctor.dc.auth_down.headline: Mojang's login servers aren't responding
packetdoctor.dc.auth_down.summary: The server couldn't check your account because the login servers are down or slow. It isn't your fault.
packetdoctor.dc.unverified.headline: Your login couldn't be verified
packetdoctor.dc.unverified.summary: The server couldn't confirm you are logged in. Your login session has probably expired.
packetdoctor.dc.unverified.note: Restarting the launcher usually renews it.
packetdoctor.dc.account_banned.headline: Your account is banned from online play
packetdoctor.dc.account_banned.summary: Mojang/Microsoft has blocked this account from multiplayer. This isn't this server's decision.
packetdoctor.dc.no_multiplayer.headline: Multiplayer is turned off for your account
packetdoctor.dc.no_multiplayer.summary: Your Microsoft account settings (often parental controls) don't allow multiplayer.
packetdoctor.dc.no_multiplayer.note: Account privacy and online safety settings.
packetdoctor.dc.login_failed.headline: Logging in failed
packetdoctor.dc.shutdown.headline: The server shut down
packetdoctor.dc.shutdown.summary: The server was stopped, probably for a restart or maintenance.
packetdoctor.dc.transferred.headline: You were sent to another server
packetdoctor.dc.transferred.summary: The server moved you to a different server%s, and that connection didn't work out.
packetdoctor.dc.config_error.headline: Setting up the connection failed
packetdoctor.dc.config_error.summary: Something went wrong while the server was sending your game its setup data. It's usually a mod present on one side but not the other.
packetdoctor.dc.player_data.headline: Your saved player data is broken
packetdoctor.dc.player_data.summary: The server couldn't load your player file (inventory, position and so on).
packetdoctor.dc.player_data.note: The server's saved data for you.
packetdoctor.dc.query_response.headline: Your game answered a question it wasn't asked
packetdoctor.dc.query_response.summary: During login your game sent a reply the server didn't expect. This is usually a mod that does its own login handshake.
packetdoctor.dc.invalid_packet.headline: The server couldn't understand what your game sent
packetdoctor.dc.invalid_packet.summary: Your game sent data the server couldn't read. This happens when your game version or mods don't match the server's.
packetdoctor.dc.invalid_packet.note: A mismatch between your game and the server.
packetdoctor.dc.timeout.headline: The connection timed out
packetdoctor.dc.timeout.summary: The server stopped answering (or your game stopped hearing it).%s This is almost always the internet connection or a frozen server.
packetdoctor.dc.timeout.silence: Nothing came from the server for the last %s seconds.
packetdoctor.dc.timeout.note: Your connection, or the server freezing.
packetdoctor.dc.custom.headline: The server disconnected you
packetdoctor.dc.custom.note: The message comes from the server or one of its plugins.
packetdoctor.dc.too_big.headline: Something was too big to send
packetdoctor.dc.too_big.summary: The server tried to send your game more data at once than Minecraft allows. It's usually an item stuffed with data (books, shulker boxes) or a very busy spot in the world.
packetdoctor.dc.too_big.note: It will keep happening until the item or block is removed.
packetdoctor.dc.conn_cut.headline: The connection was cut
packetdoctor.dc.conn_cut.summary: The connection was closed suddenly by the network or the server, without a proper goodbye.
packetdoctor.dc.conn_cut.note: Internet trouble, a firewall, or the server going down.
packetdoctor.dc.crypto.headline: The encrypted connection broke
packetdoctor.dc.crypto.summary: Minecraft encrypts its connection, and the data got scrambled on the way. Antivirus "web protection" or unstable networks can do this.
packetdoctor.dc.crypto.note: Something between you and the server changed the data.
packetdoctor.dc.encode.headline: Your game couldn't send some data
packetdoctor.dc.encode.summary: Your game failed to package data for the server. This is a bug, usually in a mod.
packetdoctor.dc.decode.headline: Your game couldn't read what the server sent
packetdoctor.dc.decode.summary: The server sent data your game couldn't understand.%s This usually means your version or mods don't match the server's.
packetdoctor.dc.decode.note: A mismatch between the server and your game.
packetdoctor.dc.closed.headline: The server closed the connection
packetdoctor.dc.closed.summary: The connection ended without any reason being given. The server may have crashed, restarted, or dropped you.
packetdoctor.dc.closed.silent: The server had also gone quiet for %s seconds before that, which points to it freezing or crashing.
packetdoctor.dc.closed.rejected: Just before, your game sent something the server may have rejected: %s.
packetdoctor.dc.packet_error.headline: Your game failed to handle a packet
packetdoctor.dc.packet_error.summary: Your game hit an error while processing %s from the server, and had to disconnect.
packetdoctor.dc.packet_error.note: An error inside your game while handling server data.
packetdoctor.dc.mod.headline: %s disconnected you
packetdoctor.dc.mod.summary: The disconnect came from %s, not from the server. It said: "%s"
packetdoctor.dc.mod.note: A mod on your side closed the connection.
packetdoctor.dc.server_mod.headline: Kicked by %s on the server
packetdoctor.dc.server_mod.summary: The server confirmed that %s removed you. Reason: "%s"
packetdoctor.dc.server_mod.note: The server runs Packet Doctor too and reported which mod did it.
packetdoctor.dc.operator.headline: A server operator kicked you
packetdoctor.dc.server_error: The server also reported an error with your connection: %s
packetdoctor.dc.generic.headline: You were disconnected
packetdoctor.dc.generic.summary: The reason given was: "%s". Packet Doctor doesn't recognise this exact message, but the details below may help.
packetdoctor.dc.connect_unknown_host.sum: Your computer couldn't find a server with that address. It may be misspelled, or the server's domain may have expired.
packetdoctor.dc.connect_unknown_host.not: The address couldn't be looked up.
packetdoctor.dc.connect_refused.headline: The server refused the connection
packetdoctor.dc.connect_refused.summary: The computer at that address is there, but nothing is accepting Minecraft connections on that port. The server is probably off or on a different port.
packetdoctor.dc.connect_timeout.headline: The server didn't answer
packetdoctor.dc.connect_timeout.summary: Your game tried to connect but got no reply. The server may be off, blocked by a firewall, or not port-forwarded.
packetdoctor.dc.connect_unreachable.head: Your computer can't reach the internet
packetdoctor.dc.connect_unreachable.summ: There is no network route to the server. Your internet connection is probably down.
packetdoctor.dc.connect_unreachable.note: A problem on your side of the connection.
packetdoctor.dc.connect_reset.headline: The connection was reset while joining
packetdoctor.dc.connect_reset.summary: The connection was cut right at the start. Firewalls, antivirus programs or the server's protection can do this.
packetdoctor.dc.connect_generic.headline: Couldn't connect to the server
packetdoctor.kick.throttle.headline: You reconnected too quickly
packetdoctor.kick.throttle.summary: The server limits how often you can join, and you tried again too soon.
packetdoctor.kick.starting.headline: The server is still starting
packetdoctor.kick.starting.summary: The server (or the proxy in front of it) isn't ready to accept players yet.
packetdoctor.kick.whitelist.headline: You aren't on this server's whitelist
packetdoctor.kick.whitelist.summary: This server only lets in players on its list, and your account isn't on it.
packetdoctor.kick.whitelist.note: The server's settings decide who can join.
packetdoctor.kick.vpn.headline: The server blocks VPNs or proxies
packetdoctor.kick.vpn.summary: The server thinks you are connecting through a VPN, proxy or hosting provider, and it doesn't allow that.
packetdoctor.kick.vpn.note: An anti-VPN plugin on the server.
packetdoctor.kick.banned.headline: You are banned from this server
packetdoctor.kick.banned.summary: The server has banned your account. You can't join until the ban ends or is lifted.
packetdoctor.kick.banned.note: The server's staff or a ban plugin decided this.
packetdoctor.kick.anticheat.headline: The server's anti-cheat kicked you
packetdoctor.kick.anticheat.summary: An anti-cheat plugin thought something you did wasn't possible in normal Minecraft. Mods that change movement, combat or building are the usual cause, but lag can trigger it too.
packetdoctor.kick.anticheat.note: An anti-cheat plugin on the server.
packetdoctor.kick.mods.headline: Your mods don't match the server
packetdoctor.kick.mods.summary: The server requires some mods you don't have, or doesn't allow some mods you do have.
packetdoctor.kick.mods.note: The server checks which mods you use.
packetdoctor.kick.version.headline: Your game version isn't supported
packetdoctor.kick.version.summary: The server (or ViaVersion on it) doesn't support the Minecraft version you're playing.
packetdoctor.kick.proxy_down.headline: The network couldn't send you to a server
packetdoctor.kick.proxy_down.summary: This server is a network (a proxy like Velocity or BungeeCord in front of several servers), and the server behind it is down or refused you.
packetdoctor.kick.proxy_down.note: A server behind the network's proxy.
packetdoctor.kick.restart.headline: The server is restarting
packetdoctor.kick.restart.summary: The server is restarting or under maintenance.
packetdoctor.kick.full.headline: The server is full
packetdoctor.kick.full.summary: Every player slot is taken. Nothing is wrong with your game.
packetdoctor.kick.auth.headline: Your login couldn't be verified
packetdoctor.kick.auth.summary: The server couldn't confirm your account is logged in.
packetdoctor.kick.auth.note: Your login session or the login servers.
packetdoctor.kick.duplicate.headline: Your account logged in somewhere else
packetdoctor.kick.duplicate.summary: The same account joined from another place, so this connection was removed.
packetdoctor.kick.duplicate.note: Only one connection per account is allowed.
packetdoctor.kick.packet_rate.headline: Your game sent too much, too fast
packetdoctor.kick.packet_rate.summary: The server has a limit on how many packets a player may send each second, and your game went over it.
packetdoctor.kick.packet_rate.note: Usually a mod or macro that clicks, moves or interacts very quickly.
packetdoctor.kick.spam.headline: Kicked for spam
packetdoctor.kick.spam.summary: You sent messages, commands or actions too quickly.
packetdoctor.kick.idle.headline: You were idle for too long
packetdoctor.kick.idle.summary: The server removes players who are away (AFK) for a while.
packetdoctor.kick.timeout.headline: The connection timed out
packetdoctor.kick.timeout.summary: The server stopped hearing from your game (or the other way round).
packetdoctor.kick.timeout.note: Your connection, or the server freezing.
packetdoctor.kick.error.headline: The server hit an error
packetdoctor.kick.error.summary: The server (or a plugin on it) had an internal error with your connection and removed you.
packetdoctor.kick.error.note: An error on the server side.
packetdoctor.kick.packets.headline: The server rejected packets from your game
packetdoctor.kick.packets.summary: The server didn't like some data your game sent. This is often a mod, but a version mismatch can also cause it.
packetdoctor.kick.kicked.headline: You were kicked
packetdoctor.kick.kicked.summary: Someone on the server (or one of its plugins) removed you.
packetdoctor.crash.debug.headline: You crashed the game on purpose
packetdoctor.crash.debug.summary: This crash was started by holding the debug crash keys (F3 + C). Nothing is broken.
packetdoctor.crash.oom.headline: The game ran out of memory
packetdoctor.crash.oom.summary: Minecraft used all the memory (RAM) it was allowed and couldn't continue. Big modpacks, high render distance and shaders use the most.
packetdoctor.crash.oom.note: Not enough memory was given to the game.
packetdoctor.crash.mixin.headline: A mod couldn't hook into the game
packetdoctor.crash.mixin.summary: %s failed to change Minecraft's code while starting. It is usually made for a different Minecraft version, or conflicts with another mod.
packetdoctor.crash.mixin.note: The mod that failed to load.
packetdoctor.crash.linkage.headline: A mod is missing something it needs
packetdoctor.crash.linkage.summary: A mod tried to use part of the game or another mod that isn't there%s. This happens when a mod is for another version or a required library is missing.%s
packetdoctor.crash.linkage.missing_mod: The missing part belongs to a mod that isn't installed.
packetdoctor.crash.linkage.note: This mod was looking for the missing part.
packetdoctor.crash.loop.headline: The game got stuck in an endless loop
packetdoctor.crash.loop.summary: Some code kept calling itself until it ran out of room (a stack overflow). This is a bug, often two mods triggering each other.
packetdoctor.crash.loop.note: A bug in a mod or the game.
packetdoctor.crash.graphics.headline: The graphics system failed
packetdoctor.crash.graphics.summary: Minecraft's drawing code hit an error from your graphics card or its driver. Old drivers, shaders and rendering mods are the usual causes.
packetdoctor.crash.cme.headline: Two things changed the same data at once
packetdoctor.crash.cme.summary: Some code changed a list while something else was reading it. This is a bug, almost always in a mod.
packetdoctor.crash.world.headline: Something in the world crashed the game
packetdoctor.crash.world.headline_server: Something in the world crashed the game's built-in server
packetdoctor.crash.world.headline_dedica: Something in the world crashed the server
packetdoctor.crash.world.summary: A block, block entity or mob in the world failed while being updated.%s The same thing will likely crash it again when that area loads.
packetdoctor.crash.world.entity: It was an entity (a mob, item or other moving object).
packetdoctor.crash.world.note: An object in the world. The technical details list where it is.
packetdoctor.crash.resources.headline: Loading textures or models failed
packetdoctor.crash.resources.summary: The game crashed while loading resources such as textures, models or sounds. A broken resource pack is the usual cause.
packetdoctor.crash.mod.headline: %s crashed the game
packetdoctor.crash.minecraft.headline: The game crashed
packetdoctor.crash.minecraft.summary: Minecraft hit an error it couldn't recover from: %s.
packetdoctor.tip.vanilla_report: Minecraft also saved a report here: %s
packetdoctor.tip.send_report: If you ask for help, click Copy report and paste it; it includes everything needed.
packetdoctor.tip.read_message: Read the message above: server messages usually say exactly what to do (wait, update, or ask staff).
packetdoctor.tip.rejoin_ask_staff: Try joining again. If it keeps happening, ask the server's staff why.
packetdoctor.tip.appeal: If you think it's a mistake, look for an appeal form on the server's website or Discord.
packetdoctor.tip.no_alts: Don't join with another account to get around a ban; that usually makes it permanent.
packetdoctor.tip.whitelist_add: Ask the server owner to add your exact username to the whitelist.
packetdoctor.tip.right_account: Check you're logged in with the right account in the launcher.
packetdoctor.tip.wait_retry: Wait a little and try again.
packetdoctor.tip.close_other_windows: Close any other Minecraft windows that use the same account.
packetdoctor.tip.secure_account: If it wasn't you, change your Microsoft account password.
packetdoctor.tip.rejoin_move: Rejoin, and move around now and then to stay active.
packetdoctor.tip.movement_mods_off: Turn off movement mods (flight, freecam that moves you, speed, no-fall).
packetdoctor.tip.lag_false_alarm: If you use no such mods, it was probably lag; rejoining is usually enough.
packetdoctor.tip.remove_movement_mods: Remove or turn off mods that change how you move.
packetdoctor.tip.retype: Type the message again yourself instead of pasting it.
packetdoctor.tip.slow_chat: Wait a few seconds between messages and commands.
packetdoctor.tip.no_auto_messages: Turn off mods or macros that send messages automatically.
packetdoctor.tip.automation_off: Turn off auto-clickers, macros and mods that act for you (auto-sort, auto-craft, fast place).
packetdoctor.tip.use_server_version: Play on the Minecraft version the server uses, or ask whether it supports yours.
packetdoctor.tip.check_server_site: The server's website or Discord usually lists the supported versions.
packetdoctor.tip.combat_mods_off: Turn off combat mods (auto-attack, kill aura, reach).
packetdoctor.tip.sync_clock: Make sure your computer's clock and time zone are set automatically.
packetdoctor.tip.restart_launcher: Close the game and the launcher, then start them again to refresh your login.
packetdoctor.tip.chat_signing_mods: If you use a chat mod (for example No Chat Reports), make sure it's up to date, or try without it.
packetdoctor.tip.tell_admin: Tell the server admin; it needs fixing on their side.
packetdoctor.tip.accept_coc: Join again and accept the rules when asked.
packetdoctor.tip.tell_owners_transfer: Tell the server owners the transfer isn't working.
packetdoctor.tip.try_again_many_mods: Try again; the second join is often faster.
packetdoctor.tip.check_speed: If it keeps happening, check your internet speed, or remove some heavy mods.
packetdoctor.tip.wait_minutes: Wait a few minutes and try again.
packetdoctor.tip.logged_in: Check you're logged in to the launcher with a Minecraft account.
packetdoctor.tip.mojang_appeal: Look up your account's status and appeal on the Minecraft website.
packetdoctor.tip.xbox_settings: Check the Xbox privacy and online safety settings for your account (or ask a parent to).
packetdoctor.tip.wait_rejoin: Wait a minute or two, then join again.
packetdoctor.tip.match_mods: Make sure you have the same mods (and mod versions) as the server.
packetdoctor.tip.admin_player_data: Ask an admin to check or reset your player data.
packetdoctor.tip.match_version_mods: Make sure your Minecraft version and mods match the server's.
packetdoctor.tip.flood_before: The server sent a flood of data just before, which can freeze your game long enough to time out.
packetdoctor.tip.check_internet: Check your internet connection (try loading a website).
packetdoctor.tip.cable_no_vpn: If you can, use a cable instead of Wi-Fi, and turn off any VPN.
packetdoctor.tip.server_lagging: If others are disconnected too, the server itself was probably frozen or lagging.
packetdoctor.tip.admin_remove_item: Ask an admin to remove the oversized item or block near where you were.
packetdoctor.tip.every_join: Until then it will probably happen every time you join or go to that place.
packetdoctor.tip.disable_ssl_scan: Turn off "HTTPS/SSL scanning" or "web protection" in your antivirus, and any VPN.
packetdoctor.tip.update_named_mod: Update the mod named above, or try without it.
packetdoctor.tip.update_mod_exact: Make sure you have exactly the version of %s the server uses.
packetdoctor.tip.install_same_version: Install %s, in the same version as the server.
packetdoctor.tip.exact_version: Use exactly the same Minecraft version as the server.
packetdoctor.tip.exact_modpack: On a modded server, use the server's exact modpack.
packetdoctor.tip.wait_check_status: Wait a minute and try again; check the server's Discord or status page.
packetdoctor.tip.one_place: If it only happens in one place, something there may be too big for the server.
packetdoctor.tip.every_server: If it happens on every server, the problem is probably your connection.
packetdoctor.tip.remove_mod_report: If that doesn't help, try without %s and report the problem to its author.
packetdoctor.tip.match_version_exact: Make sure you use exactly the server's Minecraft version and mods.
packetdoctor.tip.tell_staff_packet: Tell the server staff; the server may have sent broken data.
packetdoctor.tip.mod_same_version: If the server also uses %s, make sure both have the same version.
packetdoctor.tip.update_or_remove: Update %s, or remove it if you don't need it on this server.
packetdoctor.tip.rejoin_send_report: Try joining again; if it keeps happening, copy the report and ask for help.
packetdoctor.tip.check_address: Check the server address for typos.
packetdoctor.tip.check_site_address: Check the server's website for its current address.
packetdoctor.tip.change_dns: If other sites work, try a different DNS (for example 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8).
packetdoctor.tip.check_port: Check the port number (the part after the colon).
packetdoctor.tip.own_server_running: If it's your own server, make sure it's running.
packetdoctor.tip.wait_restart: The server may be restarting; wait a minute and try again.
packetdoctor.tip.school_network: School, work and public networks often block games; try another network.
packetdoctor.tip.port_forward: If it's your own server, check the port forwarding and firewall.
packetdoctor.tip.check_internet_vpn: Check your internet connection and any VPN.
packetdoctor.tip.disable_av: Try briefly turning off your antivirus or firewall, or a VPN.
packetdoctor.tip.check_address_online: Check the address, and check the server is online.
packetdoctor.tip.turn_off_mod: Turn off %s on this server and join again.
packetdoctor.tip.risky_mods: These installed mods are often flagged by servers: %s.
packetdoctor.tip.recent_problems: Packet Doctor saw %s serious problem(s) with what your game sent just before this; see the warnings below.
packetdoctor.tip.server_noticed: The server noticed a problem with your game just before: "%s". See the warnings below.
packetdoctor.tip.wait_10s: Wait about 10 seconds before joining again.
packetdoctor.tip.ask_owner_add: Ask the server owner to add you.
packetdoctor.tip.disable_vpn: Turn off your VPN or proxy and join again.
packetdoctor.tip.anticheat_mods_off: Turn off mods that change movement, combat, building or what you can see.
packetdoctor.tip.anticheat_lag: If you use no such mods, it was probably lag; tell the staff if it keeps happening.
packetdoctor.tip.install_server_mods: Install the mods the server asks for, in the same versions, and remove any it doesn't allow.
packetdoctor.tip.send_staff_report: Send the server staff the report (Copy report) so they can find the error.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.debug: Nothing to fix. The debug crash shortcut is F3 + C held for 10 seconds.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.more_memory: Give Minecraft more memory in your launcher's settings (Java arguments, e.g. -Xmx6G).
packetdoctor.tip.crash.more_memory_serve: Give the server more memory in its start script (the -Xmx value).
packetdoctor.tip.crash.lower_settings: Lower the render distance and turn off shaders.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.lower_view_distan: Lower the view-distance and simulation-distance in server.properties.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.half_ram: Don't give it more than about half of your computer's RAM.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.update_for_versio: Get the version of %s made for this exact Minecraft version.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.conflict: If it is already up to date, it may conflict with another mod; try removing mods added at the same time as %s.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.update_mods: Update %s to versions made for this Minecraft version.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.dependencies: Check each mod's page for required libraries (like Fabric API) and install them.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.bisect: Remove recently added mods one at a time until it stops.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.update_driver: Update your graphics card driver from NVIDIA, AMD or Intel's website.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.no_shaders: Turn off shaders and remove rendering mods to test.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.dedicated_gpu: On a laptop, make Minecraft (javaw.exe) use the dedicated graphics card.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.report_author: Report it to the mod's author with the crash report.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.backup_world: Make a backup of the world before trying anything else.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.remove_object: The technical details say where the broken object is; removing it (with a world editor or commands) usually fixes the crash.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.update_owner: Update %s, which the broken object belongs to.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.remove_packs: Remove resource packs one at a time to find the broken one.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.note_moment: Note what you were doing when it crashed; if it happens again at the same moment, that's the trigger.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.no_packs_update_f: Try without resource packs and shaders, and update Fabric Loader.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.update_fabric_ser: Update Fabric Loader and Fabric API on the server.
packetdoctor.tip.crash.share: If you ask for help, share the report (Copy report) and Minecraft's crash report.
packetdoctor.sdc.bad_data: sent data the server couldn't read: %s
packetdoctor.cmd.status: Packet Doctor %s - %s player(s) online, %s with Packet Doctor
packetdoctor.cmd.monitoring_off: Packet monitoring is turned off in config/packetdoctor-server.json.
packetdoctor.cmd.unknown_player: No player called %s has been seen since the server started.
packetdoctor.cmd.mod_yes: Their game has Packet Doctor, so they get explanations when disconnected.
packetdoctor.cmd.mod_no: Their game doesn't have Packet Doctor.
packetdoctor.cmd.traffic: From player: %s/s (%s packets, %s)  To player: %s/s (%s packets, %s)
packetdoctor.cmd.no_crash: No server crash has been recorded.
packetdoctor.cmd.alert.click: Click to see this player's details
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.huge.title: Huge packet from the server
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.huge.detail: The server sent %s at %s. Minecraft's hard limit is %s; anything near it can freeze or disconnect you.
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.huge.advice: Usually an item or block with enormous data near you. Tell an admin where you were.
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.chunk.title: Very large chunk
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.chunk.detail: A single chunk was %s. Normal chunks are well under 100 KB.
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.chunk.advice: Something nearby holds a lot of data (full chests of written books, huge builds with block entities). It can cause lag or disconnects around here.
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.items.title: Items with a lot of data
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.items.detail: %s was %s. Items packed with data (books, shulker boxes) can crash or kick players.
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.items.advice: Avoid opening the container or holding the item; tell an admin, as this is a known way to "book ban" players.
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.text.title: Very long text from the server
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.text.advice: Extremely long messages can lag your game. It's usually a plugin or someone abusing chat.
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.big.title: Big packet from the server
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.big.advice: Big packets can cause lag spikes on slow connections. If it keeps happening in one place, tell an admin.
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.payload.title: Large mod or plugin data
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.payload.detail: A mod or plugin on the server sent %s in one message.
packetdoctor.warn.in.size.payload.advice: Usually harmless (maps, resource data), but it can cause short freezes.
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.total.title: Flood of packets from the server
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.total.detail: %s packets arrived in one second, mostly: %s.
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.total.advice: Floods like this cause lag and can time you out. It's often a busy farm, a big explosion or a plugin.
packetdoctor.warn.in.transfer.title: Server transfer
packetdoctor.warn.in.transfer.detail: The server asked your game to move to %s.
packetdoctor.warn.in.transfer.advice: Normal on server networks. If you didn't expect it, note where it sent you.
packetdoctor.warn.in.channel.title: Data for a mod you don't have
packetdoctor.warn.in.channel.detail: The server sent data on the channel %s, which nothing in your game understands, so it was ignored.
packetdoctor.warn.in.channel.advice: Harmless. The server expects a mod or plugin companion ("%s") that you don't have; you only miss its extra features.
packetdoctor.warn.in.teleport.invalid.de: The server tried to teleport you to an impossible position %s.
packetdoctor.warn.in.teleport.invalid.ad: This can crash your game or corrupt your position. It's a server or plugin bug; tell an admin.
packetdoctor.warn.in.teleport.edge.title: Teleported past the world border
packetdoctor.warn.in.teleport.edge.detai: The server moved you to %s, beyond the edge of the world.
packetdoctor.warn.in.teleport.edge.advic: Moving from there will get you kicked. Ask an admin to move you back.
packetdoctor.warn.in.explode.invalid.det: An explosion at %s with size %s isn't a valid number.
packetdoctor.warn.in.explode.invalid.adv: Broken explosions are used to crash players. Tell an admin.
An explosion tried to push you by %s, which isn't a valid number.
This can break your position and get you kicked. Tell an admin.
packetdoctor.warn.in.explode.kb.title: Extreme explosion knockback
packetdoctor.warn.in.explode.kb.detail: An explosion pushed you %s blocks per tick (about %s blocks per second).
packetdoctor.warn.in.explode.kb.advice: Being flung this fast can trigger anti-cheat or fly kicks. If you didn't expect it, tell an admin.
packetdoctor.warn.in.explode.radius.deta: An explosion with size %s happened (TNT is 4).
packetdoctor.warn.in.explode.radius.advi: Explosions this big cause heavy lag. Usually a plugin or command.
packetdoctor.warn.in.particles.count.det: One particle effect asked for %s particles.
packetdoctor.warn.in.particles.count.adv: This can freeze or crash your game. Lower Particles in video settings to "Minimal" if it keeps happening.
packetdoctor.warn.in.particles.invalid.d: A particle effect had a position that isn't a valid number.
packetdoctor.warn.in.particles.invalid.a: Usually harmless, but it's a server or plugin bug.
packetdoctor.warn.in.motion.invalid.deta: The server set your speed to %s, which isn't a valid number.
packetdoctor.warn.in.motion.invalid.advi: This can break your position and get you kicked. Tell an admin.
packetdoctor.warn.in.motion.fast.title: Launched very fast
packetdoctor.warn.in.motion.fast.detail: The server launched you at about %s blocks per second.
packetdoctor.warn.in.motion.fast.advice: Flying this fast can trigger anti-cheat kicks or load chunks slowly. Usually a plugin or knockback item.
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.particles.deta: %s particle packets (%s particles) in one second.
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.particles.advi: Lower Particles in video settings. If it happens in one spot, a farm or plugin is causing it.
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.sound.title: Sound flood
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.sound.advice: Loud farms and lag machines cause this. Move away from the source.
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.explode.title: Explosion flood
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.explode.advice: Move away; this much at once causes heavy lag.
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.entities.title: Entity flood
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.entities.advic: Too many mobs or items nearby. Lower your entity distance, or move away.
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.chat.title: Chat flood
packetdoctor.warn.in.rate.chat.advice: Someone or something is spamming chat. It can lag your game.
packetdoctor.warn.in.silence.title: The server went quiet
packetdoctor.warn.in.silence.detail: Nothing has come from the server for %s seconds.
packetdoctor.warn.in.silence.advice: The server may be frozen, or your connection dropped. After about 30 seconds you'll time out.
packetdoctor.warn.in.silence.end.title: The server is back
packetdoctor.warn.in.silence.end.detail: Data started arriving again after %s seconds of silence.
packetdoctor.warn.in.silence.end.advice: That was a lag spike on the server or your connection.
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.long.title: Chat message too long
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.long.detail: Your game sent a %s-character message; the limit is 256.
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.long.advice: The server will kick you for this. A chat mod is probably removing the limit.
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.illegal.title: Character not allowed in chat
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.illegal.detai: Your message contains %s at position %s, which Minecraft doesn't allow.
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.illegal.advic: This gets you kicked. Retype the message instead of pasting it.
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.spam.title: Sending messages too fast
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.spam.detail: You're at about %s recent messages; the server kicks at 10.
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.spam.advice: Stop sending messages or commands for a few seconds, or you'll be kicked for spam.
packetdoctor.warn.out.chat.spam_soon.det: You're at about %s recent messages; the server kicks at 10.
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.invalid.title: Your game sent a broken position
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.invalid.detai: Your position isn't a valid number.
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.invalid.advic: The server kicks for this immediately. A movement mod is almost certainly the cause.
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.edge.title: Your position is outside the world
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.edge.detail: Your game said you are at %s, beyond the world limit.
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.edge.advice: The server kicks for this. Turn off movement mods.
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.far.title: Moved very far in one step
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.far.detail: Your game moved you %s blocks in one step.
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.far.advice: The server will likely pull you back ("moved too quickly"), and anti-cheats may kick you. Speed or teleport mods cause this.
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.rotation.titl: Your game sent a broken rotation
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.rotation.deta: Where you're looking isn't a valid number.
packetdoctor.warn.out.move.rotation.advi: The server kicks for this. A camera or aim mod is probably the cause.
packetdoctor.warn.out.book.title: Book too big
packetdoctor.warn.out.book.detail: Your game sent a book with %s pages, a %s-character page and a %s-character title (limits: 100, 1024, 32).
packetdoctor.warn.out.book.advice: The server rejects this and may kick you. A book-editing mod is the likely cause.
packetdoctor.warn.out.sign.title: Sign text too long
packetdoctor.warn.out.sign.detail: Your game sent a sign line %s characters long (limit 384).
packetdoctor.warn.out.sign.advice: The server rejects this. A sign mod is the likely cause.
packetdoctor.warn.out.size.title: Your game sent a big packet
packetdoctor.warn.out.size.advice: Servers often limit how much a player may send at once and can kick you for it. Usually an item with lots of data or a mod.
packetdoctor.warn.out.rate.total.title: Your game is sending a lot
packetdoctor.warn.out.rate.total.advice: Servers kick for too many packets (Paper's default limit is about 500 per second). Turn off auto-clickers and macros.
packetdoctor.warn.out.rate.move.title: Too many movement updates
packetdoctor.warn.out.rate.move.detail: %s movement packets in one second; the normal game sends 20.
packetdoctor.warn.out.rate.move.advice: This looks like a timer or speed mod to anti-cheats and can get you kicked.
packetdoctor.warn.out.rate.limit.title: Too many actions: %s
packetdoctor.warn.limit.place_recipe: Paper and Spigot servers allow only a few recipe book clicks per second and kick above that. Turn off auto-crafting mods.
packetdoctor.warn.limit.container_click: This many inventory clicks looks like an inventory mod or macro, and servers may kick for it.
packetdoctor.warn.limit.interact: Interacting with entities this fast looks like an auto-attack mod to anti-cheats.
packetdoctor.warn.limit.use_item_on: Placing or using on blocks this fast looks like a fast-place mod to anti-cheats.
packetdoctor.warn.limit.use_item: Using items this fast looks like an auto-clicker to anti-cheats.
packetdoctor.warn.limit.swing: Swinging this fast looks like an auto-clicker to anti-cheats.
packetdoctor.warn.limit.player_action: Digging or dropping this fast looks like a nuker or auto-drop mod to anti-cheats.
packetdoctor.warn.limit.set_carried_item: Switching hotbar slots this fast looks like an auto-swap mod to anti-cheats.
packetdoctor.warn.net.skipped.title: A packet was skipped
packetdoctor.warn.net.skipped.detail: Your game couldn't send or read a packet and skipped it: %s
packetdoctor.warn.net.skipped.advice: Something may now be out of sync. It usually means your mods or version don't quite match the server.
packetdoctor.warn.net.timeout.title: Connection timed out
packetdoctor.warn.net.timeout.advice: Check your internet connection; if others are affected too, the server froze.
packetdoctor.warn.net.decode.title: Couldn't read data from the server
packetdoctor.warn.net.decode.advice: This usually disconnects you. Your version or mods probably don't match the server's.
packetdoctor.warn.net.encode.title: Couldn't send data to the server
packetdoctor.warn.net.encode.advice: This is a bug in your game, usually a mod. It usually disconnects you.
packetdoctor.warn.net.io.title: Network error
packetdoctor.warn.net.io.advice: Your connection had a problem. Check your internet, Wi-Fi or VPN.
packetdoctor.warn.net.error.title: Connection error
packetdoctor.warn.net.error.advice: Something unexpected went wrong with the connection. The technical details can help a modder find it.
packetdoctor.warn.net.handle.title: Your game failed to handle a packet
packetdoctor.warn.net.handle.advice: This usually disconnects you. It's a bug in a mod, or a mismatch with the server.
packetdoctor.warn.srv.skipped.title: The server skipped a packet from your game
packetdoctor.warn.srv.skipped.detail: The server couldn't read a packet your game sent and ignored it: %s
packetdoctor.warn.srv.skipped.advice: Your version or mods probably don't quite match the server's.
packetdoctor.warn.srv.decode.title: The server couldn't read your game's data
packetdoctor.warn.srv.decode.advice: Your version or mods probably don't match the server's. Use the server's exact setup.
packetdoctor.warn.srv.handle.title: The server failed to handle your packet
packetdoctor.warn.srv.handle.advice: This is a bug on the server side (a mod or plugin), or a mismatch. Tell the server staff.
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.huge.title: Huge packet sent to the player
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.huge.detail: The server sent them %s at %s. Minecraft's hard limit is %s; they will likely be disconnected.
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.huge.advice: Usually an item or block with enormous data near the player. Find and remove it.
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.chunk.title: Very large chunk sent to the player
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.chunk.advice: Something near the player holds a lot of data (block entities, written books). It can lag or disconnect players there.
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.items.title: Items with a lot of data
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.items.advice: Oversized items (books, shulker boxes) are used to "book ban" players. Check the player's inventory and nearby containers.
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.text.title: Very long text sent to the player
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.text.advice: Usually a plugin, or a player abusing chat or signs.
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.big.title: Big packet sent to the player
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.big.advice: Big packets cause lag spikes for players on slow connections.
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.payload.title: Large mod or plugin data sent
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.payload.detai: A mod or plugin sent the player %s in one message.
packetdoctor.swarn.in.size.payload.advic: Usually harmless, but it can cause short freezes on their side.
packetdoctor.swarn.in.rate.total.title: Flood of packets to the player
packetdoctor.swarn.in.rate.total.advice: This can lag or time out the player. Look for busy farms, lag machines or plugins near them.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.chat.long.title: Chat message too long
packetdoctor.swarn.out.chat.long.detail: Their game sent a %s-character message; the limit is 256.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.chat.long.advice: A modified or hacked client; vanilla can't send this.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.chat.illegal.advi: Usually pasted text; Minecraft kicks them for it.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.invalid.deta: Their position isn't a valid number.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.invalid.advi: Only modified clients send this; it's a known crash attempt. Minecraft kicks them.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.edge.title: Position outside the world
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.edge.detail: Their game said they are at %s.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.edge.advice: Only modified clients send this. Minecraft kicks them.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.far.title: Moved very far in one step
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.far.detail: They moved %s blocks in one step.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.far.advice: Could be lag, elytra or a teleport mod. Worth watching if it repeats.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.rotation.det: Their look direction isn't a valid number.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.move.rotation.adv: Only modified clients send this. Minecraft kicks them.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.book.title: Oversized book
packetdoctor.swarn.out.book.detail: They sent a book with %s pages, a %s-character page and a %s-character title (limits: 100, 1024, 32).
packetdoctor.swarn.out.book.advice: Vanilla can't send this; it's a known way to create oversized items.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.sign.title: Sign text too long
packetdoctor.swarn.out.sign.detail: They sent a sign line %s characters long (limit 384).
packetdoctor.swarn.out.size.title: Player sent a big packet
packetdoctor.swarn.out.size.advice: Large packets from players are rare; it's usually an item with lots of data or a modified client.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.rate.total.title: Player is sending a lot
packetdoctor.swarn.out.rate.total.advice: Macros, auto-clickers or a modified client. It can lag the server.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.rate.move.title: Too many movement updates
packetdoctor.swarn.out.rate.move.detail: %s movement packets in one second; the normal game sends 20.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.rate.move.advice: Often a timer or speed mod, but a lag spike on their side can also cause a burst.
packetdoctor.swarn.out.rate.limit.title: Too many actions: %s
packetdoctor.swarn.limit.place_recipe: Rapid recipe book clicks are a known way to lag servers. Auto-crafting mods also do it.
packetdoctor.swarn.limit.container_click: Inventory mods, macros or dupe attempts.
packetdoctor.swarn.limit.player_action: Possibly a nuker or auto-drop mod.
packetdoctor.swarn.srv.skipped.title: Skipped a packet from the player
packetdoctor.swarn.srv.skipped.detail: The server couldn't read one of their packets and ignored it: %s
packetdoctor.swarn.srv.skipped.advice: Their version or mods probably don't match the server's.
packetdoctor.swarn.srv.decode.title: Couldn't read the player's data
packetdoctor.swarn.srv.decode.advice: A version or mod mismatch, or a modified client sending garbage. They will be disconnected.
packetdoctor.swarn.srv.handle.title: Failed to handle the player's packet
packetdoctor.swarn.srv.handle.advice: A bug in a server mod (named if found), or a malformed packet. The technical details are in the server log.
